title: Writ identifiers and references (v1)
description: Globally unique object identifiers, repository designators, and cross-repository references. Normative text: spec/identifiers.md. Cross-field invariants the schema cannot express (opaque-fallback handling) are defined in the spec text and enforced by validators alongside this schema. additionalProperties is deliberately never false: unknown fields are preserved and ignored.

person-id.description: Person identifier: scheme ":" value, split on the FIRST colon (an email value may carry a colon in a quoted local part), per spec/identifiers.md. The scheme matches [a-z][a-z0-9+.-]* and is at most 32 characters; the value is 1 to 320 code points, excluding the forbidden code points spec/identifiers.md section Value character repertoire names (C0/C1 controls, DEL, bidi controls/isolates/embeddings/overrides, and zero-width/invisible characters, including the BOM). There is no bare, colonless form and no implicit scheme. maxLength 353 is derived (32 + 1 + 320) and stated so a validator seeing only the flat string has a number. The length bound is a resource cap, not an RFC 5321 conformance check: Writ does not parse email addresses. Bounds are enforced by rejection, never truncation. The value bound applies to the normalized value, which producers MUST have written. The unit is Unicode code points, not octets and not UTF-16 code units; the corpus brackets the bound in all three under spec/testdata/persons/. The pattern's forbidden-code-point ranges are written as JSON \u escapes, so the decoded pattern carries the literal code points themselves and behaves identically under Go's regexp and an ECMA-262 engine. spec/identifiers.md section Value shape: Stream-Safe Text additionally requires a conforming producer to refuse a value whose NFD carries a run of more than 30 consecutive non-starters (Canonical_Combining_Class != 0), per UAX #15 section 13 Stream-Safe Text Format. That rule is producer-enforced only and is not reflected in this pattern: ECMA-262 has no Canonical_Combining_Class property escape, and \p{Mn} is not the same set, so this schema alone cannot reject such a value. As with the repertoire rule above, this is a necessary check, not a sufficient one.

object-id.description: Canonical Writ-minted object ID: 128 bits of entropy as 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters.

repo-id.description: Writ repository designator: 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters minted at writ init.

reference.description: Reference string: optional 32-hex repo-id followed by #, followed by an object-id (canonical 32-hex or envelope-legal opaque ASCII without #). maxLength 289 is derived (32 + 1 + 256) and counts code points, not octets and not UTF-16 code units; the pattern's second half admits non-ASCII, so the three units disagree here and the bound is bracketed in all of them under spec/testdata/references/. Enforced by rejection, never truncation: a truncated reference points at a different object. Normative text: spec/identifiers.md §Length bound.

canonical-reference.description: Canonical reference: bare <object-id> (32 hex) or <repo-id>#<object-id> (32 hex # 32 hex).
